title: Halls and parks where Bolden played
summary: Jones names Masonic Hall, Valley Hall, Jackson Street Hall, St. Elizabeth Hall, Lincoln Park, Johnson Park and Providence Hall, and tells of Bolden calling his children home from Johnson Park.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Can you tell us where he played? Where did he give dances? Where were the dances when you heard Bowling? What hall, where did you go to hear him?

Well, the Masonic Hall, and the, uh, the, uh, the, uh, the, uh, the, uh, the, uh, the place is, it's broke up now. The Valley Hall? The Valley? The Valley Hall used to be on Party Street. It used to be on Party Street.
I wonder if that's the Mississippi Valley Hall. Oh, no, no, no, no.
And, uh, Jackson Street Hall used to be here. That over there?
The one right across, uh, the... That just burned?
Huh?
Yeah. The one that just burned, huh? I don't know. The one that, the, the hall that just... The hall just got burnt.
It wasn't...
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah. Call it Long, used to call it Long Shumming Hall.

Yeah, uh-huh. And they used to play St. Elizabeth Hall. Mm-hmm. We folks, we St. Elizabeth Hall on Couch Street up there. Up there, up there, somewhere above Napoleon Avenue. And they used to play Lincoln Park.
Mm-hmm.
And sometimes, sometimes they'll be, they went to the background.
Would they play at, uh, in the day, or the night, or what time?
They're called, they're always at night. Nearly always at night.
Mm-hmm. How was Lincoln Park? Did they play in the day there in Lincoln Park though, or just at night there too?
Night.
Night.
And the fairgrounds at night too? Mm-hmm.

They used to play in the, you know what you call them, like the art people that give them a picnic. They had both day and night. That's the way they used to play. And they used to play that way as Lincoln Park. And they used to be, maybe you called it Long Island, remember Johnson Park?
Yeah, so I don't remember, it was right next to Lincoln Park.

Yeah, right next to Lincoln Park. Well, they used to play in that. That's why Buddy Bolton used to say, to Carnies and them, say, Carnies, come on. Put your head, put your head through the window. Put your carnage out there. He said, I'm going to call my children home. He'd be at Johnson Park. Mm-hmm. Robeshoe would be at Lincoln Park. Buddy Bolton started praying too, and all the people out at Lincoln Park, come on. Come on, know where Buddy Bolton was.

Any particular tune he'd play at that time, or just anything? Who? Was there any particular song he played at that time? You know, when he's calling his children home, would he have a special song he'd play?

Oh, I don't know about that. I didn't ask that particular. Yeah, I just wondered. He was one of the loudest and the most loud, greatest loud player they had at that time, regardless of where they were calling.
Do you remember Providence Hall? There's a building, it's a church right over here someplace now. Who? Was it called Providence Hall, Old Providence Hall? I know. On Phillip Street. Wait, wait.
That's here, Phillip and Living. A brick church right there.
That's the one, isn't it? Yeah, that's it.
That's why Old Providence Hall used to be. That's why Buddy Bolton used to play in that too.
